question: In which year was the Bengal Partition of 1905 reversed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1911**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bengal Partition of 1905, implemented by Lord Curzon, divided Bengal into East Bengal and West Bengal based on religious demographics.
 
• It was reversed in **1911** due to widespread protests, boycotts, and the Swadeshi Movement led by Indian nationalists.
 
• The reversal coincided with the shifting of the capital of British India from Calcutta (now Kolkata) to Delhi in the same year.
 
• The annulment was seen as a victory for Indian nationalism but led to further communal tensions in the region.
 
• After 1911, Bengal was reunited as a single province under British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**

 
 
• Implemented by Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, to improve administration efficiency.
 
• It divided Bengal into East Bengal (Muslim-majority) and West Bengal (Hindu-majority).
 
• The move was criticized as a deliberate attempt to divide Hindus and Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• Launched as a protest against the partition, promoting the boycott of British goods and the use of Indian-made products.
 
• Key leaders included Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
• It played a significant role in the rise of Indian nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Delhi as Capital:**
 
 
• In 1911, the British shifted the capital from Calcutta to Delhi to strengthen their imperial control.
 
• Delhi was considered geographically strategic for administrative purposes.
 
• The coronation of King George V in Delhi marked this significant change.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Reversal:**
 
 
• While the reversal of Bengal's partition was celebrated, it sowed seeds of communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims.
 
• It eventually contributed to the broader demand for separate electorates and later, the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
